records.label: spacr.power_model.scan_parameters#2
records.source: **A point that fails is reported as failed.**  A fit that raises lands as ``status="failed"`` with the exception text in ``error``; a fit that runs but does not meet its convergence criterion lands as ``status="not_converged"``.  Both carry ``NaN`` metrics.  This is the whole point: a sweep that backfilled 0.5 for its broken points would plot as a design sitting at chance, and "this design cannot find its hits" and "this fit crashed" are conclusions with opposite consequences.
records.context: **A point that fails is reported as failed.**  A fit that raises lands as ``status="failed"`` with the exception text in ``error``; a fit that executes but does not meet its convergence criterion lands as ``status="not_converged"``.  Both carry ``NaN`` metrics.  This is the whole point: a sweep that backfilled 0.5 for its broken points would plot as a design sitting at chance, and "this design cannot find its hits" and "this fit crashed" are conclusions with opposite consequences.
records.translation: **Un punto que falla se registra como fallido.** Un ajuste que genera una excepción termina con ``status="failed"`` y el texto de la excepción en ``error``; un ajuste que se ejecuta pero no satisface su criterio de convergencia termina con ``status="not_converged"``. Ambos llevan métricas ``NaN``. Esa es la finalidad: un barrido que asignara 0.5 a sus puntos defectuosos se representaría como un diseño al nivel del azar, pero "este diseño no puede encontrar sus aciertos" y "this fit crashed" son conclusiones con consecuencias opuestas.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#5
records.source: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1 — the "fast" version would get slower the further you scrolled. Only tables with no usable key (views, composite-primary-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.context: **Use keyset paging instead of OFFSET.** Fetch each chunk with ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite scan every skipped row, so chunk 500 costs about 500× as much as chunk 1 and the "fast" version gets slower. Small views and composite-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables have no usable row key and use ``OFFSET`` as a fallback.
records.translation: **Paginación por clave, no OFFSET.** Cada bloque solicita ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` y ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` hace que SQLite recorra (y descarte) cada fila omitida, por lo que el bloque 500 de una tabla de 400 k filas costaría 500× lo que cuesta el bloque 1 — la versión "fast" se volvería más lenta cuanto más se avanzara. Solo las tablas sin una clave utilizable (vistas y tablas ``WITHOUT ROWID`` con clave primaria compuesta) recurren a ``OFFSET``, y por construcción son pequeñas.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.home#2
records.source: 1. **The first tab is everything, in the same categories as the rest.** Home is not a summary of the other tabs — it holds every app, at a density that fits one screen, banded by the *same* sections the category tabs use. It used to band them into Prepare / Run / Review instead, a second grouping that existed nowhere else: an app read as "Prepare" on the first tab and "Data" on the second, and adding a section meant editing two tables that could disagree. There is one table now (:data:`spacr.qt.app.APPS`) and both the bands and the tabs are computed from it, by the *registry*, and handed in — this widget takes ``categories`` and ``bands`` already grouped and does not know what a section means.
records.context: 1. **The first tab is everything, in the same categories as the rest.** Home is not a summary of the other tabs — it holds every app, at a density that fits one application view, banded by the *same* sections the category tabs use. It used to band them into Prepare / Run / Review instead, a second grouping that existed nowhere else: an app read as "Prepare" on the first tab and "Data" on the second, and adding a section meant editing two tables that could disagree. There is one table now (:data:`spacr.qt.app.APPS`) and both the bands and the tabs are computed from it, by the *registry*, and handed in — this widget takes ``categories`` and ``bands`` already grouped and does not know what a section means.
records.translation: 1. **La primera pestaña lo contiene todo, en las mismas categorías que el resto.** Home no es un resumen de las otras pestañas — contiene todas las aplicaciones, con una densidad que cabe en una vista de la aplicación, organizadas en las *mismas* secciones que usan las pestañas de categorías. Antes las agrupaba en Preparar / Ejecutar / Revisar, una segunda agrupación que no existía en ningún otro lugar: una aplicación aparecía como "Prepare" en la primera pestaña y como "Data" en la segunda, y añadir una sección obligaba a editar dos tablas que podían discrepar. Ahora existe una sola tabla (:data:`spacr.qt.app.APPS`); tanto las bandas como las pestañas se calculan a partir de ella mediante el *registro* y se entregan ya preparadas — este widget recibe ``categories`` y ``bands`` ya agrupados y no sabe qué significa una sección.

records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** A run used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the run that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** A processing session used to be untraceable. The log said a field failed; the registry said an artifact existed; nothing connected them, so "show me everything from the processing session that produced this file" had no answer. :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, which is the whole point.
records.translation: **Un identificador de sesión de procesamiento en cada línea de registro y en cada salida.** Antes, una sesión de procesamiento no podía rastrearse. El registro indicaba que un campo había fallado; el registro de artefactos indicaba que existía un artefacto; nada los conectaba, de modo que "muéstrame todo lo correspondiente a la sesión de procesamiento que produjo este archivo" no tenía respuesta. :func:`run_context` crea un identificador, lo estampa en cada :class:`logging.LogRecord` creado en cualquier parte del proceso, escribe un registro JSONL por sesión de procesamiento que :func:`read_run_log` vuelve a leer y entrega el *mismo* identificador a :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. Así, una línea de registro y una salida se pueden relacionar mediante ``run_id``; esa es toda la finalidad.
